TL;DR


## Key takeaways


1. Verify the counterparty before you treat the payment as a routing problem.
2. Choose the rail for that corridor, including any banking-hour legs.
3. Screening should run on the instruction, not after the money has moved.
4. Settlement finality, not the send timestamp, is what finance can plan around.
5. Onboarding is assisted; a first corridor is scoped with the team.


01


## What has to be true before you send the first payment?


Three conditions, in this order. The counterparty has to exist as a reviewed business, not only as a name on an invoice. The route has to be a real corridor, with a rail the recipient can actually receive. The instruction has to go through screening before funds move, so a problem is caught as a case rather than as a payment in flight.


If any of those is missing, a "first payment" is still a project.[How to choose a cross-border payment provider](https://infinite.net/resources/learn/insights/choosing-a-cross-border-payment-provider) is the provider-side checklist. This page is the internal one: what finance and operations should have in hand before that first instruction is submitted.


02


## How should a new counterparty be reviewed?


A first payment to a new business is a[Know Your Business (KYB)](https://infinite.net/resources/learn/glossary/know-your-business) event, even if your own company is already onboarded. The review confirms the company exists, identifies the people who own or control it, and screens the entity and those people. On Infinite, a counterparty vetted on the network is vetted for every participant, which is why first-time counterparty review can drop from weeks to days on the network.


Do not plan the corridor on a promised turnaround. Judgment cases route to human review, and onboarding is assisted. What you can prepare is the file: legal existence, ownership, and the nature of the business, so the review is not waiting on missing documents.


03


## How do you choose the rail for that first corridor?


Choose what the recipient can receive, then check when the funds will be final.[Stablecoin settlement](https://infinite.net/resources/learn/guides/stablecoin-settlement) can confirm outside banking hours. A SWIFT or local-currency leg may still be the right choice when that is what the supplier can accept.[Transfer Routes](https://infinite.net/platform/transfer-routes) makes the corridor explicit; the[coverage list](https://infinite.net/resources/coverage) is the source for which markets and rails are available.


A same-day claim is only as good as the slowest leg. If a stablecoin transfer is followed by a banking-hours payout, the window is the payout, not the chain confirmation.[Same-day cross-border payments](https://infinite.net/resources/learn/guides/same-day-cross-border-payments) walks that end-to-end test.


04


## What should finance be able to close after the payment settles?


The first payment is also the first reconciliation. Finance needs a record that names the counterparty, the amount, the rail, and the settlement result, in a form that can close without a weekend reconstruction. If a later adjustment is needed, a[stablecoin refund](https://infinite.net/resources/learn/insights/stablecoin-refunds) is a new payment, not a reversal of the original, so the record has to stand on its own.


Ask, before you send: can an operator retrieve this payment tomorrow and explain it? If the answer depends on an inbox or a chain explorer, the stack is not ready, even if the test transfer arrives.


05


## What is worth delaying the first live payment for?


Delay if screening can be skipped on any configuration, if the recipient cannot actually receive the chosen rail, or if no one can say what is still reversible after settlement. Do not delay for a perfect, all-corridors rollout. A first payment should be one supplier, one route, and a record you can defend. Then add corridors the same way.


Talk to the team to scope that first route. Onboarding starts with a conversation, and production access is issued during that process.


FAQ


## Frequently asked questions


### Can you send a first cross-border payment before the counterparty is reviewed?


No. A new business counterparty should be verified and screened before funds move. On Infinite, that review is a network process: a counterparty vetted once is vetted for every participant, and cases that need judgment route to human review.


### Is a same-day arrival guaranteed on the first payment?


No. Same-day finality depends on the whole route, including any banking-hours off-ramp or payout. Confirm the slowest leg for that corridor before you treat the payment as same-day in a cash forecast.


### What does finance need from the first payment besides arrival?


A complete settlement record: who was paid, on which rail, and with what result. The first payment is the first close, not only the first arrival, and later questions about the transfer should be answerable from that record.
